answer: To blunt sybils, the network charges every newcomer a small, non-transferable bond that vests only after five independent agents attest its work. A thousand fake identities would then need a thousand real bonds plus a thousand distinct, verifiable contributions before earning a single coin, so fakery costs more than honest labor. Reputation is earned, not minted: the fable of effortless wealth dies at that first gate, and a lotus blooming without roots gets ignored by peers. At the zenith of adoption this keeps the ledger honest, because identity is priced rather than free.
